newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians reject US stand on Arab land dealers.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians reject US stand on Arab land dealers.

text.p: Palestinian officials on Wednesday rejected U.S. legislators' condemnation of the killing of Arabs who sold land to Israelis.
Israel welcomed the comments made on Tuesday by U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich that those responsible for the killings were acting like Nazis.
Gingrich also threatened to block aid to the Palestinian Authority if its leaders failed to denounce the killings.
"Mr Gingrich is fully aware that the Palestinian Authority will not allow people to take the law into their own hands," said top Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat.

"This is a disgusting thing and these positions are aimed at destroying the peace process and for a few votes here and there, the American Congress allows the bloodshed of Palestinians and Israelis," Erekat told Reuters.
Three Arab land dealers have been killed since the Palestinian Authority last month revived a Jordanian law banning land sales to Jews, an offense punishable by death.
Palestinian Justice Minister Freih Abu Medeen was quoted on May 4 as saying that Palestinians who sold land to Jews faced execution.
Israel has alleged the Palestinian Authority had ties to the killings. The authority has denied any involvement.

"We welcome the recognition of what is happening here by the Congress of the U.S.," David Bar-Illan, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's media adviser, told Reuters, commenting on Gingrich's remarks.
Palestinian police on Tuesday detained Hussein Ilayan al-Sawadeh, who heads their military intelligence in the West Bank town of Ramallah, on suspicion of misuse of authority.
Israel Radio reported that Sawadeh was suspected of involvement in the land dealers' killings.

Gingrich said in an emotional floor speech: "The Palestinians must be on notice that these senseless actions must stop. The vigilante murder of realtors by Palestinian security officials is an egregious violation of human rights and of international norms."
Gingrich was speaking on a "Sense of Congress" amendment, which expresses the House's opinion but does not make law.

The amendment, to a bill funding State Department operations, was passed on a voice vote. The United States has pledged $500 million in aid to the Palestinians over five years, of which $220 million has already been distributed.

The State Department deplored the killing of the land dealers and said it was outrageous for the death penalty to be imposed for such an act. But is has said Washington plans to continue giving the pledged aid.
"This is the kind of action we identify with Nazis. This is the kind of racist activity that this planet holds to be reprehensible and unacceptable," Gingrich said.
A succession of Republican and Democratic legislators rose to support Gingrich in a debate marked by unanimity.
